item.title: Australia’s Privacy Regulator Beginning 2026 With Its First Compliance Sweep
item.description: The Office of the Australian Information Commissioner (OAIC), Australia’s privacy regulator, is conducting its first ever privacy compliance sweep, as of this January. The compliance sweep will include a review of the privacy policies of businesses that collect information in person. The OAIC is focusing on businesses in industries with practices that involve the in-person collection of personal information. item.title: 26 Insights for Employers Sponsoring Immigration Applications in 2026
item.description: Despite heightened scrutiny, evolving adjudication standards, and continued operational pressure on U.S. immigration agencies, 2026 may prove a viable — and even advantageous — year for U.S. employers to sponsor global talent. item.title: FTC Attorneys Ask Court to Hold Payment Processors in Contempt for Allegedly Violating 2015 Order
item.description: On June 13, 2026, the Federal Trade Commission requested a federal court to hold the operators of a payment processing operation in contempt for alleged systematic violations of a 2015 order with the agency over allegations they illegally processed credit card payments. item.title: Thought Leadership for Lawyers: Education, Not Promotion
item.description: In the legal profession, the phrase thought leadership is often misunderstood, particularly when it comes to publishing articles and providing commentary as third-source experts. For many attorneys, contributing to public discourse can feel uncomfortably close to self-promotion or marketing, activities that may seem misaligned with a profession grounded in discretion, ethics, and credibility. item.title: The Chemicals Omnibus File and the Use of CMRs in Cosmetics- a First Halt to Simplification?
item.description: The European Parliament and the Council are shaping their positions on the Chemicals Omnibus simplification proposal published by the Commission on 8 July 2025. Discussions on the text are expected to be heated, with an important involvement of civil society groups. item.title: Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) – Adoption of Operational Rules and Proposal to Extend the Scope
item.description: In the context of the transition to the definitive CBAM regime as from 1 January 2026, the European Commission adopted, in December 2025, a package of implementing and delegated acts, together with a proposal to amend Regulation (EU) 2023/956 in order to extend the scope of CBAM to certain downstream products and to introduce additional anti-circumvention measures. item.title: Court Approves Order Requiring Disney to Pay $10MM to Settle FTC Attorney Allegations of Unlawful Collection of Children’s Personal Data
item.description: On December 31, 2025, the FTC announced that a federal judge approved an order requiring Disney to pay $10 million to settle Federal Trade Commission allegations that the company allowed personal data to be collected from children who viewed child-directed videos on YouTube without notifying parents or obtaining their consent as required by the Children’s Online Privacy Protection Rule (COPPA Rule). item.title: Reputation (High Court’s Version)- Bed Bath ‘N’ Table v Global Retail Brands Australia
item.description: The High Court of Australia has allowed Bed Bath ‘N’ Table Pty Ltd’s (BBNT) appeal from the decision of the Full Federal Court in its case against Global Retail Brands Australia Pty Ltd (GRBA).1 The key takeaway for businesses is that a finding against trade mark infringement does not prevent liability under the Australian Consumer Law (ACL).
